label: bug
file: src/ingest/parser.ts

The new Windows export tool almost certainly produces CRLF (`\r\n`) line endings. `parseStatement` only splits on `"\n"`, so each line (including the header) keeps a trailing `\r`. That makes the last header column come out as `description\r` instead of `description`, so `REQUIRED_COLUMNS.every(...)` fails and `assertShape` throws `errors.rowShape` for the header row itself — which is why it's always reported as "row 1" regardless of the file contents. The parser needs to strip trailing `\r` from each line (or split on `/\r?\n/`) before processing.

file: src/ingest/parser.ts

The new Windows export tool almost certainly produces CRLF (`\r\n`) line endings. `parseStatement` only splits on `"\n"`, so each line (including the header) keeps a trailing `\r`. That makes the last header column come out as `description\r` instead of `description`, so `REQUIRED_COLUMNS.every(...)` fails and `assertShape` throws `errors.rowShape` for the header row itself — which is why it's always reported as "row 1" regardless of the file contents. The parser needs to strip trailing `\r` from each line (or split on `/\r?\n/`) before processing.
